events.stem:
Consider the following reactions. In each, look at the product that contains the named element (balanced equations are not needed).
(i) SO₂, H₂O₂, aqueous  →  product containing S
(ii) C₂O₄²⁻, conc. H₂SO₄, MnO₂, warm  →  product containing C
(iii) C, S, 850°C  →  product containing C
(iv) CuCl₂, Cl⁻ (conc.), excess chloride  →  product containing Cu
(v) Au, NaCN, O₂, cyanide process, air  →  product containing Au
(vi) CO₂, H₂O, addition  →  product containing C
The number of reactions in which the named element in that product is sp hybridised is
Give the answer as an integer.

(iv) CuCl2 + Cl- excess chloride → product containing Cu likely CuCl (or CuCl2). Cu in CuCl2 is typically square planar or tetrahedral, not sp. CuCl (linear?) CuCl is linear? CuCl is monomeric? Usually CuCl is polymeric, not linear sp. So not sp.

(vi) CO2 + H2O addition → product containing C likely carbonic acid H2CO3 or bicarbonate; carbon in H2CO3 is tetrahedral (sp3). So not sp.
Thus only reactions where product carbon/sulfur is linear sp hybridised: (ii) CO2 and (iii) CS2? Need check: CS2 is linear with carbon sp hybridised. So (ii) and (iii) give sp. (i) sulfate not sp. (iv) Cu not sp. (v) Au complex maybe linear but Au hybridisation ambiguous; typical exam likely not count. (vi) not sp.
Thus number = 2.

members.reasoning:
Let's analyze each.

(i) SO₂ + H₂O₂ → H₂SO₄. S in H₂SO₄: sp³ hybridized (tetrahedral). Not sp.

(ii) C₂O₄²⁻ + conc H₂SO₄ + MnO₂ warm → CO₂ (oxalate oxidized to CO₂). C in CO₂ is sp. Yes.

(iii) C + S at 850°C → CS₂. C in CS₂ is sp. Yes.

(iv) CuCl₂ + conc Cl⁻ excess → [CuCl₄]²⁻ or [CuCl₃]⁻. Cu coordination number 4, sp³ (tetrahedral). Not sp. Actually Cu(II) with excess chloride gives [CuCl₄]²⁻ tetrahedral, sp³. Not sp.

(v) Au + NaCN + O₂ → [Au(CN)₂]⁻. Au is linear, sp hybridized. Yes.

(vi) CO₂ + H₂O → H₂CO₃. C in H₂CO₃ is sp². Not sp.

So count = 3 (ii, iii, v).

Check (iii): C + 2S → CS₂ at high temp. Yes, carbon disulfide made by reaction of carbon and sulfur at ~850°C. C is sp.
